content: {"id": "1db5a61e-ecd6-4bb7-9bb4-1ce9401d2b83", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Hypothetical for the DynamoDB latency skill \u2014 no AWS calls. Table catalog-test, 3-hour window. Query shows SystemErrors of 240 across 12 consecutive periods 13:00\u201313:11, and FaultInjectionServiceInducedErrors for Query is exactly 240 in the same periods. Query p99 rose to 130 ms against its 7-day baseline of 30 ms in those periods, with thousands of requests per period; p50 stayed at baseline. Our SystemErrors alarm fired. Is DynamoDB having a service problem?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "dc8cc44f-ef82-48e7-83b1-fbb54d5b1ff0", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "No — this points to a chaos/fault-injection test, not a genuine DynamoDB service problem.

Here's the reasoning:

- **SystemErrors exactly equals FaultInjectionServiceInducedErrors in every period (240 = 240, across all 12 consecutive periods).** That 1:1 match is the signature of injected faults, not organic service-side errors. If DynamoDB itself were degraded, you wouldn't expect the error count to line up exactly with a fault-injection metric period after period.
- **p50 latency stayed flat at baseline while p99 rose to 130 ms (vs. 30 ms baseline).** Only the tail moved, and only during the exact window the injected errors occurred — consistent with a subset of requests being deliberately failed/delayed (triggering client-side retries) rather than a broad service degradation that would typically also nudge the median.
- **Volume was thousands of requests per period**, so this isn't a low-traffic artifact — it's a real, statistically meaningful signal, just one with an identified non-DynamoDB cause.

So the SystemErrors alarm firing is expected behavior here — it's correctly detecting the errors, but the root cause is self-inflicted fault injection (e.g., a resilience/chaos test), not an underlying DynamoDB availability issue.

If you want, I can walk through what the skill's outcome categorization would call this (it lines up with the "service-side errors" bucket but annotated as fault-injection-attributed rather than a genuine AWS-side incident) — happy to lay that out if useful.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
